item.title: Explicit bounds for the number of solutions to Roth-type inequalities over adelic curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.06973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we provide an upper bound on the number of a special system of Roth-type Diophantine inequalities over proper adelic curves. By refining the technique from previous work, we successfully eliminate the large-height restriction on the solutions. Furthermore, the constraints on the parameters within the inequality are further relaxed. We also give a constructive quantitative generalization of the Vojta-Dolce-Zucconi system, replacing compactness-based extraction by a discrete pigeonhole argument and a finite grid partition, so that the resulting bound has explicit dependence on the relevant parameters.
item.dc:creator: YuXi Li, GuanHeng Zhao

item.title: Metallic Circles: Concyclic Tangency Points of Ford Circles over $k$-Fibonacci Quotients
item.description: arXiv:2611.07141v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extending a result of Kocik, we show that the tangency points of the Ford circles built over quotients of $k$-Fibonacci numbers are concyclic: they lie on a circle centred on the horizontal axis, of radius $\sqrt{k^2+4}/2$, meeting it at the reciprocal of the metallic ratio $\sigma_k$ and at $-\sigma_k$. Concyclicity turns out to be a quadratic identity of the sequence read in coordinates. In the Poincar\'e half-plane, this circle is a geodesic along which the tangency points advance with constant step $2\ln\sigma_k$.
item.dc:creator: Nicol\'as Pi\~na

item.title: Mahler's Problem on Liouville Numbers II. Rational Maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.07177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1984, Mahler asked which analytic functions map the set $\mathscr L$ of Liouville numbers into itself. In the first paper of this series, we proved that every real-analytic solution on an open interval is the restriction of a real rational function. We now identify a canonical subfield $\mathbb L$ of $\mathbb R$ such that, for every nonconstant $R\in\mathbb R(X)$ and every nonempty open interval $I$ in its domain, $R(I\cap\mathscr L)\subseteq\mathscr L$ if and only if $R$ is defined over $\mathbb L$ and $R^{-1}(\mathbb Q)\cap I\cap\mathscr L=\varnothing$. The weaker inclusion $R(I\cap\mathscr L)\subseteq\mathbb Q\cup\mathscr L$ holds if and only if $R$ is defined over $\mathbb L$. If $R$ is not defined over $\mathbb L$, every such interval contains a Cantor set of Liouville numbers whose images under $R$ are irrational and have irrationality exponents bounded by a constant depending only on $R$. We also construct continuum many positive strong Liouville numbers $\sigma$ for which $\sigma X^m$ preserves $\mathscr L$ for every $m\geq2$, with all nonzero rational fibers consisting of $U_m$-numbers.
item.dc:creator: Diego Marques

item.title: On Amoebas and the Arithmetic Rigidity of the Mahler Measure
item.description: arXiv:2611.07181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a geometric rigidity theory for Mahler measure based on the global structure of Ronkin functions and amoebas. Our starting point is the theorem of Ronkin describing the affine linearity of the Ronkin function on the complement of the amoeba and the identification of its gradients with lattice points of the Newton polytope. Combining this deep analytic input with convex duality and toric geometry, we show that the vanishing of the Mahler measure is an extremal phenomenon: it occurs if and only if the Ronkin function collapses to the piecewise linear support function of the Newton polytope. This collapse forces a degeneration of the amoeba onto the $(n\!-\!1)$-skeleton of a toric fan and implies that the zero locus of the polynomial is contained in a translate of a codimension-one subtorus. As a first application of this rigidity principle, we recover the generalized Kronecker theorem characterizing Laurent polynomials of vanishing Mahler measure. Our approach bypasses the classical Boyd--Lawton limit formulas and replaces analytic projection arguments by a global convex-geometric and potential-theoretic mechanism rooted in the geometry of amoebas.
item.dc:creator: Mounir Hajli

item.title: Fields Generated by a Single Point on Elliptic Curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.07259v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the finite extensions of a number field generated by a single point on an elliptic curve. We construct geometrically non-isomorphic elliptic curves with complex multiplication that generate the same collection of extensions, giving a negative answer to a question of Mazur and Rubin. For torsion-generated fields, we prove that inclusion of the collections up to finitely many exceptions implies isogeny over the ground field, and in the non-CM case even isomorphism. When all geometric endomorphisms are defined over the ground field, we characterize equality of the torsion-generated collections by the existence, for every prime $p$, of an isogeny over the ground field of degree prime to $p$. This condition also implies equality of the full collections of fields generated by a single point.
item.dc:creator: Minseok Kim, Myungjun Yu

item.title: On explicit units in a family of cubic fields and the arithmetic of curves arising from powers of these units
item.description: arXiv:2611.07333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an integer $b\neq0,1$ let $K_b$ be the cubic field generated by the unique real root of $x^3-3bx-b^3$, let $\eta_0$ be its fundamental unit, and let $\eta_b$ be the explicit unit studied in the companion paper (arXiv:2609.37389). Write $\eta_b=\eta_0^{n(b)}$. Deciding whether $n(b)$ is divisible by $q$ amounts to finding the integral points of a plane curve $C_q$ of degree $2q$. We prove that for every integer $q\ge1$ the curve $C_q$ is irreducible with $g(C_q)=\binom{q-1}{2}$, the genus of a smooth plane curve of degree $q$ rather than of degree $2q$. The proof is not a genus computation but a structural one: $C_q$ is the inverse image, under the $q$-power map of a two-dimensional torus, of the curve traced by the minimal polynomial of $\eta_b$ as $b$ varies, and the formula falls out of two applications of Riemann-Hurwitz in the resulting tower. As a consequence the problem splits into exactly three regimes: $q=2$ rational, $q=3$ elliptic, and $q\ge4$ of general type. In particular only finitely many $b$ have $q\mid n(b)$ for each $q\ge4$. A lower bound for linear forms in two logarithms gives $n(b)<6082138$ for every $b$, so $n(b)\in\{1,2\}$ for all but finitely many $b$, though not effectively. We add two computations: $n(b)$ is determined outright for $|b|\le10^{30}$, and the rational points of $C_4$ are determined by quadratic Chabauty, giving $4\mid n(b)\iff b\in\{-75,-3,5,96\}$. We state precisely which parts of the latter rest on certified arithmetic and which do not. Finally, we show that $K_b\cong K_{b'}$ with $b\neq b'$ holds for $\{b,b'\}=\{-1,5\}$, and otherwise only if one of the two parameters, $c$ say, satisfies $|c|>10^{30}$ and $n(c)$ is divisible by a prime $q\ge5$. There are only finitely many such pairs.
item.dc:creator: Iwao Kimura, Hikaru Umemoto

item.title: Periodic counting, carry synchronization, and primes in nonstandard numeration systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.07446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $b\ge2$ be an integer and let $D\subset\mathbb{N}_0$ be a finite digit set containing zero, with maximum residue multiplicity $\mu=\max_{0\le r<b}\#\{d\in D:d\equiv r\pmod b\}$ and cardinality $q=\#D\ge2$. Under the condition $\mu<q$, we prove that the summatory representation function satisfies an asymptotic formula with a strictly positive, H\"older continuous, $1$-periodic fluctuating profile and an error of $O_D(x^{\log_b\mu})$. An exact periodic factorization of the Laplace generating function furnishes an explicit, computable Fourier expansion for the periodic profile via Gamma factors, and yields the meromorphic continuation of the associated Dirichlet series to the entire complex plane. When $D$ is a complete residue system modulo $b$, we establish an arithmetic synchronization criterion showing that the associated finite carry system admits a zero-synchronizing word if and only if $\gcd(D)=1$. This synchronization yields an exponentially accurate interval approximation and a general transfer principle for arithmetic weights. Consequently, we derive a prime number theorem for representable primes governed by the same periodic profile, alongside an exponentially convergent measurable scaling limit of the representable sets.
item.dc:creator: Nian Hong Zhou

item.title: On a problem due to Erd\H{o}s concerning $w_1(n)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.07617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adopting notation from Erd\H{o}s [Congress. Numer., 1980], we define $w_1(n) = w(n)$ for positive integers $n$ so that $w(1) = 0$ and so that: If $n > 1$ and $n = \prod p^{\alpha_p}$, then $w(n) = \sum_{p^{\alpha_p} \parallel n} \frac{n}{p^{\alpha_p}}$. By then defining $V(x)=\bigl|\{w(n):1\le n\le x\}\bigr|$ for $x \geq 1$, Erd\H{o}s considered whether or not $V(x) = o(x)$ and left this as an open problem. This same problem was also given as an open problem in Guy's famous textbook on unsolved problems in number theory and seems to have remained open. We solve this problem by proving that $V(x) \neq o(x)$, and, moreover, by proving the stronger result such that $\liminf_{x \to \infty} \frac{V(x)}{x} > 0$.
item.dc:creator: John M. Campbell

item.title: Multivariable Congruence Jumping: Periodic States, Integral Realizations, and Descent
item.description: arXiv:2611.07625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Congruence jumping replaces coordinates by integer quotients and updates polynomial divisibility relations. We extend this procedure to several variables and retain integer coefficients by recording their common factor separately. For three-variable systems of divisibilities with signed binomial numerators, we classify all positive integer exponent tuples of period at most two under three successive coordinate jumps: seven fixed tuples and twenty-two cycles of exact period two. No odd period greater than one occurs. At the chosen representatives of the twenty-two exponent two-cycles, there are eighty-four returning sign assignments. All have realizations with nonzero pairwise-coprime integer coordinates, and exactly seventy-four have such realizations with every coordinate positive throughout the six jumps. Explicit constructions and congruence arguments establish this classification. We also study jumps that decrease a specified height, distinguishing points that admit no immediate decrease from minima of entire connected components of the jump graph. For the four-variable family $Q_\lambda(x,y,z,w)=kxyzw$, where $Q_\lambda$ is the sum of the four squares plus $\lambda$ times the six pairwise products, finite bounds give complete classifications for $\lambda=1,2,3$. For $\lambda=1$, positive integer solutions exist exactly for $k=2,8,10$. These results distinguish returns of the polynomial data from integrality and positivity of the coordinate sequences.
item.dc:creator: Max A. Alekseyev, Dmitry I. Khomovsky

item.title: A Hypergeometric RM Surface: Integral Monodromy and Level-11 Covers
item.description: arXiv:2611.07849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a genus-two hypergeometric family whose Jacobians have real multiplication by $\Q(\sqrt5)$. We identify the relevant primitive factor and integral rank-two monodromy; at one real embedding the projective image is $\Delta(2,5,\infty)$, while the conjugate image is nondiscrete. At the primes above $11$, the degree-$12$ Borel covers are quadratic pullbacks of genus-one triangular modular curves. The same rank-two systems have finite-field hypergeometric Frobenius traces, yielding the local Euler factors and a quadratic transformation twisted by the character of $2$.
item.dc:creator: Devendra Tiwari

item.title: The minimal excludant and the least $r$-gaps of $\ell$-regular partitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.07871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The minimal excludant (mex) of an integer partition $\lambda$ is the smallest positive integer that is not a part of $\lambda$. In this paper we study an analogue of this statistic for $\ell$-regular partitions with $\ell\geq2$, that is, partitions in which no part is divisible by $\ell$. Recently, Meher \cite{Meher} defined the minimal excludant for $\ell$-regular partitions. Motivated by Meher \cite{Meher}, for an $\ell$-regular partition we define its least $r$-gap as the smallest positive integer not divisible by $\ell$ that appears fewer than $r$ times as a part, and we obtain the two-variable generating function for the number of $\ell$-regular partitions of $n$ with a given least $r$-gap. Let $\sigma^{\mex}_{\ell}(n)$, and $\sigma^{\mex}_{\ell,r}(n)$ be the sum of the of the mex values over all $\ell$-regular partitions of $n$ and least $r$-gaps over all $\ell$-regular partitions of $n$ respectively. Using Jacobi's triple product identity, we derive explicit expressions for the generating function of $\sigma^{\mex}_{\ell}(n)$, and $\sigma^{\mex}_{\ell,r}(n)$, with separate formulas for even and odd $\ell$. We also show that the sequence $\{\sigma^{\mex}_{\ell,r}(n)\}_{n\ge0}$ is weakly increasing for every $\ell\ge2$ and $r\ge1$. Also, using Ingham's Tauberian theorem, we establish Hardy--Ramanujan type asymptotic formulas for $\sigma^{\mex}_{\ell,r}(n)$ when $\ell=4,5,7$ and $r\ge1$ is arbitrary. Lastly, we prove $\sigma^{\mex}_{\ell,r}$ is odd infinitely often, and we establish a quantitative lower bound, showing that the number of such n up to X grows at least like log log X.
item.dc:creator: Tejash Priya, Sourav Bhowmick, Nabin Kumar Meher

item.title: Towards a twistless converse theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.07921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a finiteness theorem for Dirichlet series satisfying the Euler product, analytic continuation, and functional equation expected of a holomorphic newform. For any fixed level $N$, even weight $k$, and exponent $\sigma$, only finitely many such series have Dirichlet coefficients $\ll n^\sigma$. No hypotheses on twists by Dirichlet characters are assumed. The proof combines a combinatorial spanning theorem for Ramanujan sums with an operator-theoretic argument that uses two distinct primes to establish discreteness of the possible Hecke eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Andrew R. Booker, Min Lee, Nina Zubrilina

item.title: On Sufficient Conditions for Rank Zero in Families of Elliptic Curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.08029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we study the Mordell Weil ranks of elliptic curves in the family $E_D:y^2=x^3+Dx$, where $D\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. Under suitable congruence conditions on $D$ and its prime divisors, we use $2$-descent via a rational $2$-isogeny to study the rank of $E_D$. Under our congruence hypotheses, the ranks of these matrices give sufficient conditions for $E_D$ to have rank zero. We give explicit sufficient conditions for the curves $E_D$ to have Mordell Weil rank zero over $\mathbb{Q}$ in the following cases: (i) $D$ is an odd negative integer, (ii) $D$ is an odd positive integer, and (iii) $D$ is a positive even integer. Also we give a quantitative result describing how many square free parameters satisfy the required matrix-rank condition. In particular, our results show that these rank zero criteria hold for a significant proportion of the admissible parameters.
item.dc:creator: Shamik Das, Debajyoti De, Arup Mondal

item.title: Overholonomicity of Overconvergent $F$-isocrystals over Laurent Series Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.08193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that $K$-valued overconvergent $F$-isocrystals over smooth $k((t))$-varieties are overholonomic and construct the triangulated category of overholonomic complexes of Frobenius type which is stable under six operations and contains overconvergent $F$-isocrsytals.
item.dc:creator: Yuanmin Liu

item.title: Arithmetic theta products and doubling at arbitrary level
item.description: arXiv:2611.08243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an arithmetic doubling identity for the standard arithmetic theta series on $X_0(N)$ at arbitrary positive level, with constant $\psi(N)/24$ for the fixed genus-two Eisenstein series. The product comparison covers all pairs of integral indices. At rank zero, an explicit Epstein zeta correction agrees with the middle Bruhat orbit of the Eisenstein derivative. The common-component calculation combines integral CM adjunction, the cyclic difference divisor, and compact Green-current identities. It retains the different, conductor, internal contacts, and proportionality contacts at every prime, including dyadic and supersingular places. Finite intersections, curvature, and discriminant heights identify the nonpositive coefficients with an explicit modular completion. Uniform estimates for parameter derivatives give strong Fourier convergence. Green-energy estimates justify the double Petersson pairing. The full cusp lift exists as a Bochner integral and equals its Mordell--Weil projection. For $\mathbb Z/(2N)\mathbb Z$, explicit prime-power recursions determine the complete zero-component trace spectrum, including the dyadic factor. They give the scalar-to-vector Petersson norm correction and an isometric normalization on the active subspace. The Bruinier--Yang theorem then yields the scalar height formula on the specified Jacobi newform line. We also prove a double Rankin--Selberg criterion based on positive diagonal coefficients and record the paired analytic factorization with its ramified local integrals retained explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Tuoping Du

item.title: Density and holes of the visible points in certain cut-and-project sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.08257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the set of visible points from the origin in certain cut-and-project sets, specifically the density of the set. We generalize to all real quadratic number fields the formulas for the density found by G. Hammarhjelm, and the corresponding error bounds proved by I. Gringlaz, R. Kumar, B. Weiss. We also find the possible densities of the set of visible points in the cut-and-project set, with a constant generic lattice, and a changing window with constant volume. We also study bounds for the distance of large holes in the set of visible points of certain cut-and-project sets, generalizing theorems originally proved by P. Erd\H{o}s for $\mathbb{Z}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Hayim David Shamir

item.title: $p$-parity conjecture for Panchishkin Galois representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.08316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $V_1$ and $V_2$ be symplectic self-dual $p$-adic de Rham representations of $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ that are pure (of weight $-1$) and satisfy the Panchishkin condition at $p$. Suppose that $V_1$ and $V_2$ are residually isomorphic, compatibly with their Panchishkin filtrations. We prove the relative $p$-parity conjecture relating the ratio of the global root numbers of $V_1$ and $V_2$ to the difference of their Bloch-Kato Selmer dimensions. We have no restriction on the dimension of the Galois representation, the Hodge-Tate weights or the monodromy operator at $p$, and the residual isomorphism need not be symplectic. The proof expresses ratios of local root numbers in terms of local invariants over the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension: a new invariant introduced at $p$, and local Iwasawa $\lambda$-invariants at $\ell\neq p$. Both are compatible with the arithmetic local constants of Mazur-Rubin and Nekov\'a\v{r}. A key input, proved using Sen theory, is that the Bloch-Kato and strict local conditions at $p$ coincide over the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension, generalising results of Coates-Greenberg and Nekov\'a\v{r}. As applications, we obtain new cases of the $p$-parity conjecture, including cases of rank greater than two: Artin twists of CM Hida families, orthogonal Artin twists of ordinary modular forms, symmetric cubes along Hida families, and families of abelian surfaces, together with unconditional numerical examples.
item.dc:creator: Subham Garai, Somnath Jha, Sudhanshu Shekhar

item.title: Pointless K3 surfaces over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.08356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that K3 surfaces with no rational points over the finite field with $q$ elements exist if and only if $q \leq 11$. Our approach applies linear programming techniques to improve on generic sphere packing bounds for the discriminants of even rootless definite lattices. These bounds are applied to constrain the possible zeta functions of K3 surfaces with no rational points via the Artin--Tate formula. The remaining cases are ruled out by direct analysis of primitive embeddings of particular lattices into Niemeier lattices.
item.dc:creator: Asher Auel, Philip Engel, Kiran S. Kedlaya, Sair Shaikh

item.title: An extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37
item.description: arXiv:2611.07138v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct an extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37, resolving the last undetermined optimal minimum in ranks at most 48. The construction begins with the Cayley table of $\mathbb{Z}/13\mathbb{Z}$, assigning a vector of norm four to each cell. We prove that the resulting incidence lattice has exactly 26 unimodular completions of minimum four, all isometric. The resulting Cayley lattice $\Lambda$ has automorphism group $\mathrm{AGL}(1,13)\times C_6$ and is $s$-extremal, with shadow minimum $13/4$ and kissing number $35\,594$. An explicit $4$-frame in $\Lambda$ yields a Type I self-dual $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$-code of length 37 and minimum Euclidean weight 16, resolving the corresponding open case in coding theory.
item.dc:creator: Eric Kubischta

item.title: Gaps in the Most Frequent Sizes of Integer Sumsets
item.description: arXiv:2611.07303v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Nathanson observed that, for four-element sets $A$ of integers, the most frequent sizes of the iterated sumset $hA$ are separated by triangular numbers. Senger proved this and suggested an analogue for larger sets. We establish this pattern for $k$-element subsets of $\{1,\ldots,q\}$, for every fixed $k\geq3$, where $h\geq2$ is either fixed or grows slower than $q^{1/(2k-1)}$. As $q\to\infty$, almost every such set has the largest possible $h$-fold sumset, and almost every exception has one of $h-1$ explicit smaller sizes. The differences between consecutive sizes among these $h$ values are consecutive $(k-2)$-dimensional simplex numbers.
item.dc:creator: Saad A. Awan, Steven J. Miller, Linh Nguyen, Steven Senger, Elvis Wong

item.title: Brauer groups of generalised Markoff surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.07454v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero with $a,b,c\in k^\times$ and let $m\in k\setminus\{0,4abc\}$. We compute the Brauer group of the generalised Markoff surface $ax^2+by^2+cz^2-xyz=m$. We also construct several counterexamples to the integral Hasse principle, which are explained by the Brauer--Manin obstruction.
item.dc:creator: Zheshuai Tian, Dasheng Wei

item.title: Combinatorics of noncommutative harmonic oscillator determinant
item.description: arXiv:2611.07626v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain an explicit evaluation of the determinants that appear in the denominators of the integrands for the iterated integrals expressing special values of the spectral zeta function of the noncommutative harmonic oscillator at integers greater than 1. The determinants in question are those of cyclic tridiagonal matrices; their explicit evaluation is carried out, in addition to the inclusion-exclusion principle, conceptionally using combinatorial arguments based on monomer-dimer systems. This explicit evaluation serves as a core component in the study of arithmetic properties such as the modularity of the special values of the spectral zeta function.
item.dc:creator: Masato Wakayama, Wadim Zudilin

item.title: Anti-ribbon shaped Young diagram decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2611.07715v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a sliding procedure on diagrams which splits the standard Young tableaux of a corner-crossed diagram, in particular of a skew shape, along a finite binary tree whose leaves are anti-ribbon diagrams. Combined with standardization, this yields a decomposition of semi-standard Young tableaux into tableaux of anti-ribbon shape, indexed by standard tableaux and governed by their descent sets. As applications, we obtain expansions of Schur functions and Schur multiple zeta functions in terms of their anti-ribbon type analogues; at the level of Schur functions, this is a tableau-level form of Gessel's fundamental quasisymmetric expansion.
item.dc:creator: Hideki Murahara, Maki Nakasuji, Wataru Takeda

item.title: The parity of the number of missing integers in partitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.07908v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Missing integers in partitions have been studied by many authors. A missing integer of a partition is a positive integer smaller than its largest part that does not occur as a part. We investigate parity biases for the number of missing integers in partitions and overpartitions. For every integer $c\ge2$, we prove that the coefficients $a_c(n)$ of $(-cq;q)_\infty/(-q;q)_\infty$ are eventually strictly positive and provide an effectively computable threshold. The proof uses the circle method, combining a saddle-point analysis on the major arc with explicit uniform estimates on the minor arcs. Specializing to $c=2$ and $c=3$, and verifying the remaining finite cases, we show that partitions and overpartitions of $n$ with an even number of missing integers outnumber those with an odd number for $n>34$ and $n>27$, respectively. We further prove that, for $n>10$, the difference between the numbers of ordinary partitions with an even and an odd number of missing integers is smaller than the number of partitions of $n$ into distinct parts. These results confirm three conjectures of Bhoria, Eyyunni and Santra. We also give a combinatorial interpretation of $a_c(n)$ for every integer $c\ge4$ in terms of colored partitions, generalizing the partition and overpartition interpretations of Bhoria, Eyyunni and Santra for $c=2$ and $c=3$, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Julia Q. D. Du, Gurinder Singh

item.title: The Calkin--Wilf problems on $\ell$-ary partition functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.08109v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In their 1998 precursor to their celebrated paper ``Recounting the rationals,'' Calkin and Wilf listed nine open problems related to the function $b_{k,\ell}(n)$, the number of partitions of $n$ into powers of $\ell$ with each part appearing at most $k$ times. In this short paper, we answer five of their eight remaining open problems. As a consequence of our results, we extend and generalise results of both Carlitz and Reznick, and answer an open question of Reznick.
item.dc:creator: Michael Coons

item.title: Counting multigeodesics and the Selberg-Delange method
item.description: arXiv:2611.08165v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the counting function $\mathcal{P}^m(X,x)$ for $m$-multigeodesics of length at most $x$ on a compact hyperbolic surface $X$ where $m$ is a positive integer. Building on the Selberg-Delange method, originally developed for counting integers with exactly $m$ prime factors in the interval $[1,x]$, we prove a large $x$ asymptotic for $\mathcal{P}^m(X,x)$. We show that for fixed $m$ as $x\to\infty$ the asymptotic is independent of the surface, whereas for $\frac{m}{\log x}$ bounded away from zero, the asymptotic depends on an infinite Euler product over the lengths of primitive closed geodesics. We also study the distribution of the function $\omega_1$, defined on multigeodesics $\Gamma$ as $\omega_1(\Gamma)=k-1$ for $\Gamma=(\gamma_1,...,\gamma_k)$ a $k$-multigeodesic. We show that as $x\to\infty$, the distribution of $\omega_1$ in the set of multigeodesics of length $\leq x$ is close to that of a Poisson random variable with parameter $\log x$. Both of these theorems rely on studying the generating function of the random variable $\omega_1$ which we relate to the Selberg zeta function.
item.dc:creator: Aapo Karvonen

item.title: Fermat quotients with CM Jacobians and trivial automorphism group
item.description: arXiv:2611.08176v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $F_n$ be the Fermat curve of degree $n$ over $\mathbb Q$, and let $D_n=F_n/S_3$ be its quotient by coordinate permutations. We prove that $D_n$ has trivial geometric automorphism group for every $n\ge 11$ with $\gcd(n,6)=1$. Its Jacobian has complex multiplication. For $n=11$, this Jacobian is absolutely simple of dimension five. We construct an isogeny over $\mathbb Q$ of degree $11^5$ from $\operatorname{Jac}(D_{11})$ to the Jacobian of $y^{11}=x(1-x)^2$. For primes $p\equiv 1\pmod 3$, we also consider the metacyclic quotients $C_p$ of $F_p$ over $\mathbb Q$. By a theorem of Carocca, Lange and Rodr\'iguez, their Jacobians are absolutely simple and have complex multiplication. We prove that $C_p$ has trivial geometric automorphism group if and only if $p\ge 19$. Write $p=r^2+rs+s^2$ with $r,s$ positive integers. The natural degree-three cover $Y_p\to C_p$ satisfies $\operatorname{gon}(Y_p)=r+s$, so $\operatorname{gon}(C_p)\ge \lceil(r+s)/3\rceil$. Since $g(C_p)=(p-1)/6$, both the genus and the gonality of $C_p$ tend to infinity with $p$.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Tafazolian

item.title: Steinberg module and top-dimensional cohomology for arithmetic Chevalley groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.08381v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that for a Chevalley--Demazure group scheme $\mathcal{G}$ of type $G_2$, $F_4$ or $E_8$ and a Euclidean ring $\mathcal{O}$ with field of fractions $K$, the Steinberg module of $\mathcal{G}(K)$ is generated by integral apartment classes. As a consequence, the top-dimensional rational cohomology of $\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{O})$ vanishes if $\mathcal{O}$ is a ring of integers, extending results of T\'oth and of Br\"uck--Santos Rego--Sroka.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Gentili

item.title: A Collatz-type conjecture on the set of rational numbers (revised and extended version)
item.description: arXiv:1010.3692v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\theta(x)=(x-1)/3$ if $x\ge1$ and $\theta(x)=2x/(1-x)$ if $0\le x<1$. We conjecture that the $\theta$-orbit of every nonnegative rational number ends in $0$. A weaker conjecture asserts that no map in the semigroup generated by $3x+1$ and $x/(x+2)$, other than the generators' powers, has a positive rational fixed point; equivalently, the only matrices in the semigroup generated by $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}3&1\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\1&2\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ with an integer eigenvalue are their pure powers. We prove sharp two-sided bounds for the smallest eigenvalue of every word in the more general semigroups attached to the maps $\varphi_{a,b}$, which explain why the pair $\{2,3\}$ is distinguished: it is the only pair with $(a-1)(b-1)=2$. Combining these bounds with congruences for the trace, we determine the possible integer eigenvalues of words, and we prove that $\theta$ has no rational $1$-circuits, no rational $2$-circuits and no even rational circuits. We show that, for each $k$, a random $k$-syllable word with exponents at most $M$ has an integer eigenvalue with probability at most $2k(k+\log_2 2k)/M$. Finally, we verify by computer that $\theta$ has no positive rational cycle of length at most $36$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, A Collatz-type conjecture on the set of rational numbers, J. Number Theory 132 (2012), no. 11, 2582--2594
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: Dense 2-generator subsemigroups of $2\times 2$ matrices (revised and extended version)
item.description: arXiv:1104.5054v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the semigroup of real linear fractional transformations of a proper subinterval of the real line does not contain a dense subsemigroup generated by two elements, while it does contain dense subsemigroups generated by three elements. For the semigroup generated by the two maps $x\mapsto 1+a/x$ and $x\mapsto x/b$ (the only pair not excluded by elementary arguments) we compute the closure exactly, and we describe all of its orbit closures in the plane. Consequently the semigroup of $2\times2$ matrices with nonnegative entries has no dense $2$-generator subsemigroup but has dense $3$-generator ones. In contrast, we prove a general density criterion for subsemigroups of $M_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $M_2(\mathbb{C})$ generated by three explicit matrices, and use a word identity of length seven to produce, for both $\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{C}$, uncountable families of pairs of matrices that generate dense subsemigroups; a fully explicit rational example is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1/2\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\0&-8/3\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Thus the minimal number of generators of a dense subsemigroup is $3$ for the nonnegative cone and $2$ for $M_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $M_2(\mathbb{C})$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, Dense 2-generator subsemigroups of 2x2 matrices, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 387 (2012), 103--113
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: On the representation functions of certain numeration systems
item.description: arXiv:2305.00792v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\beta>1$ be fixed. We consider the $(\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D})$-numeration system, where the base sequence $\mathbf{b}=(b_k)_{k\geq 0}$ consists of positive real numbers satisfying $\lim_{k\rightarrow \infty}b_{k+1}/b_k=\beta$, and the digit set $\mathcal{D}\ni 0$ is a finite set of nonnegative real numbers containing at least two elements. Let $r_{\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D}}(\lambda)$ denote the number of representations of a given $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ in the form $\sum_{k\ge 0}\delta_kb_k$ with digits $\delta_k\in \mathcal{D}$. We establish upper bounds for $r_{\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D}}(\lambda)$ as well as asymptotic formulas for its arbitrary moments. Furthermore, we prove that the associated Dirichlet series $\zeta_{\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D}}(s):=\sum_{\lambda>0}r_{\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D}}(\lambda)\lambda^{-s}$ admits a meromorphic continuation to the entire complex plane when $b_k=\beta^{k}$, and to the half-plane $\mathrm{Re}(s)>\log_\beta \mathcal{D}-\gamma$ when $b_k=\beta^{k}+O(\beta^{(1-\gamma)k})$ for any fixed $\gamma\in(0,1]$. Within the regions of continuation, we determine all candidate poles, compute their corresponding residues, and locate the trivial zeros of $\zeta_{\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D}}(s)$. As an application, we resolve several problems posed by Chow and Slattery concerning partitions into distinct terms of certain integer sequences.
item.dc:creator: Nian Hong Zhou

item.title: Optimal expansion in unitary groups I: Golden adelic groups and cutoff
item.description: arXiv:2509.09047v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper and its companion [DEP2] we construct and study special generating sets for $p$-arithmetic unitary Lie groups, extending the seminal works of Lubotzky, Phillips and Sarnak to higher dimensions. The real embeddings of our sets form optimal topological generators for compact unitary Lie groups, and their $p$-adic embeddings give rise to Cayley graphs and complexes over finite unitary groups, which exhibit the cutoff phenomenon. In the current paper we prove two main results: First, we construct $p$-arithmetic lattices in $PU_4$ and $PU_8$ which act transitively on their corresponding Bruhat-Tits buildings. These groups are used to construct Golden Gate sets on two and three qubits, which have optimal circuit length and efficient compiling algorithms. Second, we study the cutoff phenomenon for quotients of the Bruhat-Tits building of a general semisimple $p$-adic group. We show that cutoff occurs for quotients which satisfy either the Ramanujan property or the weaker Sarnak-Xue Density Hypothesis (SXDH). For this purpose we bound the operator norms of a large class of Hecke operators in terms of the rate of decay of unitary representations. In the companion paper [DEP2], we prove such a SXDH result for unitary groups.
item.dc:creator: Rahul Dalal, Shai Evra, Ori Parzanchevski

item.title: A note on general isolation result in Diophantine Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2509.25628v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the present paper we give very simple general statements which deal with approximation of a real number by rationals and are related to isolation phenomenon. In particular we study functions $ f(x)>f_1(x)>0$ such that existence of solutions $\frac{p}{q}$ of Diophantine inequality $ \left| \alpha -\frac{p}{q}\right|< \frac{f(q)}{q^2} $ leads to the existence of solutions of inequality $ \left| \alpha -\frac{p}{q}\right|< \frac{f_1(q)}{q^2} $.
item.dc:creator: Sergei Pitcyn, Nikolay Moshchevitin

item.title: Generalized Hausdorff measure of irrationals with Lagrange value exactly 3
item.description: arXiv:2511.10328v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the generalized Hausdorff measure of some natural subsets of $k^{-1}(3)$, where $k^{-1}(3)$ consists of the real numbers $x$ for which $\left| x-\frac{p}{q} \right|<\frac{1}{(3+\varepsilon)q^2}$ has infinitely many rational solutions $\frac{p}{q}$ for any $\varepsilon<0$ but only finitely many for any $\varepsilon>0$. It is well known that $k^{-1}(3)$ is an uncountable set with Hausdorff dimension zero. Given any dimension function $h$, we determine the exact ``cut point" at which the generalized Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^h(k^{-1}(3))$ drops from infinity to zero. In particular we show that such a measure is always zero or not $\sigma$--finite, and, as an application, we can classify topologically $k^{-1}(3)$. Moreover, we show that the subset of attainable elements of $k^{-1}(3)$ has the same generalized Hausdorff measure as $k^{-1}(3)$, but the subset of non--attainable elements of $k^{-1}(3)$ has a ``strictly smaller" generalized Hausdorff measure.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Gustavo Moreira, Harold Erazo, Nicolas Angelini

item.title: The infinitude of square-free palindromes
item.description: arXiv:2601.07097v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We settle an open problem regarding palindromes; that is, positive integers which are the same when written forwards and backwards. In particular, we prove that for any fixed base $b\geq 2$, there exist infinitely many square-free palindromes in base $b$. We also provide an asymptotic expression for the number of such integers $\leq x$. The core of our proof utilises a hybrid $p$-adic/Archimedean van der Corput process, used in conjunction with an equidistribution estimate of Tuxanidy and Panario, as well as an elementary argument of Cilleruelo, Luca and Shparlinski.
item.dc:creator: Daniel R. Johnston, Bryce Kerr

item.title: Torsion points on $\rm{GL}_2$-type abelian varieties
item.description: arXiv:2602.21047v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is well known that the order of the torsion group of an abelian variety over a number field divides the greatest common divisor of the sizes of points on the reduction at each prime (except for an explicit finite set). Drawing inspiration from Katz's Inventiones paper (1981), we investigate the converse to this for abelian varieties of \(\rm GL_2\)-type and exhibit a tentative list of possible rational torsion orders for modular abelian varieties over \(\mathbb Q\) of dimension up to \(5\).
item.dc:creator: Jessica Alessandr\`i, Nirvana Coppola

item.title: Semistable Reduction Theorem for Overconvergent $F$-isocrystals over Laurent Series Fields
item.description: arXiv:2604.17799v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the semistable reduction theorem for $\mathcal{E}^{\dag}_K$-valued and $K$-valued overconvergent $F$-isocrystals over $k((t))$-varieties which were introduced by Lazda and P\'{a}l. As an application, we prove the finite dimensionality of $\mathcal{E}^{\dag}_K$-valued rigid cohomology with compact support.
item.dc:creator: Yuanmin Liu

item.title: Irrationality exponents of logarithms of positive rational numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.10192v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study rational approximation to logarithms of positive rational numbers and give a separated-weight determinant argument for $\mu(\log r)=2$ whenever $r\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\setminus\{1\}$. The geometric input is an interpolation theorem for logarithmic jets at points with distinct multiplicative coordinates. Its successive weight thresholds are independent of the interpolation centres; the eventual degree threshold may depend on them. A local intersection-length bound and a curve inequality lead to surjectivity through a blow-up and Serre vanishing. For a fixed rational argument, this produces a nonzero rational determinant. Clearing denominators gives an arithmetic lower bound, while an exact row translation and repeated Taylor indices yield a contradictory analytic upper bound. The consequences include nonzero rational linear combinations of such logarithms, rational affine changes, and logarithms of positive numbers with a rational positive integer power. We also give a bounded-fibre interpolation extension, an explicit bound for the final analytic degree, and a counterexample to interpolation under the volume condition alone.
item.dc:creator: Jingwen Liu, Kai Jiang, Pingwen Zhang

item.title: A zero-density estimate for the symmetric square $L$-functions in the weight aspect
item.description: arXiv:2610.37371v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove a zero-density estimate for the symmetric square $L$-functions associated with Hecke eigencuspforms in the weight aspect. The proofs are based on the mollified second moment of these $L$-functions.
item.dc:creator: Songchen Yin

item.title: Smooth numbers in simultaneous arithmetic progressions
item.description: arXiv:2611.01522v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a mean value theorem on the distribution of smooth numbers in two simultaneous arithmetic progressions, with generalizing a result of Drappeau. Let $\varepsilon>0$ and $(\log x)^C<y<x^{1/C}$ for a sufficiently large $C$. Our result implies that $y$-smooth numbers are well-distributed in the residue classes of a fixed integer $a$ on average over moduli $\leq x^{5/9-\varepsilon}$ and $\leq x^{153/256-\varepsilon}$ for each $|a|\leq x$, which improves Drappeau's range $\leq x^{6/11-\varepsilon}$. As an application, we show that a positive proportion of $y$-smooth numbers $n\leq x$ satisfy $\min(P^+(n-1), P^+(n+1))>x^{407/720}$.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyuan Yang

item.title: The module structure of ideals in degree $p$ extensions of $p$-adic fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.02301v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $L/K$ be a degree $p$ extension of $p$-adic fields. We shall provide a complete characterization for the freeness of any fractional ideal $\mathfrak{p}_L^h$, $h\in\mathbb{Z}$, of $L$ as a module over its associated order $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$ in the only Hopf-Galois structure on $L/K$, and an explicit description of $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$. We show that there is no loss of generality in assuming that $0\leq h\leq p-1$ and that the normal closure of $L/K$ is totally ramified over $K$. If $L/K$ is maximally ramified, then $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$ is the maximal $\mathcal{O}_K$-order in $H$ and $\mathfrak{p}_L^h$ is $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$-free. The remaining cases correspond to typical extensions. For these, we provide an $\mathcal{O}_K$-basis of $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$ and a characterization for the condition that $\mathfrak{p}_L^h$ is $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$-free. In the non-exceptional cases, which had been partially studied in the Galois setting, the characterization depends on $h$ and the continued fraction expansion of $\frac{a}{p}$, where $a$ is the residue class mod $p$ of the (fractional) ramification jump $\ell$ of $L/K$. In the remaining exceptional case, where $L/K$ is almost maximally ramified and $a+1\leq h\leq p-1$, it consists in a numerical common minimizer condition.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Gil-Mu\~noz

item.title: A normalization issue in a transmitted form of Bloch's diamond formula: anti-invariant subgroup versus regulator quotient
item.description: arXiv:2611.05420v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bloch's regulator formula for an elliptic curve is often quoted with a generator of the anti-invariant subgroup $H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})^-$ and coefficient $1$ in front of the elliptic dilogarithm of the diamond product. We compare this wording with Brunault's published intersection-product formula. The natural map from the anti-invariant subgroup to the regulator quotient $H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})/H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})^+$ has index $1$ when $E(\mathbb{R})$ has two components and index $2$ when it has one. Thus, up to orientation, the coefficient is $1$ for a quotient generator and $\iota(E)\in\{1,2\}$ for a subgroup generator. This is an elementary consequence of the published formula, not a new regulator theorem. We illustrate the distinction on 11.a3 using an externally proved regulator anchor and the Brunault--Bertin special values, and on 20.a4 by high-precision numerical integration. We also correct our earlier quotation of Touafek: his printed identity is $\pi r=D_E((f)\diamond(g))$, with $r=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{\gamma^-}\eta$. It is compatible with the subgroup normalization when $\Delta<0$; when $\Delta>0$ the corresponding coefficient is $1/2$, up to orientation. We do not reassess his isogeny theorem or his final exotic relation here. No new proof of Boyd's conductor-11 split-integral identity is included.
item.dc:creator: Huimin Zheng

item.title: Spherical Cap $L_2$ Discrepancy -- Blessing of Dimensionality and a Distance-Kernel Variant
item.description: arXiv:2604.21340v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a dimension-explicit upper bound for the information-complexity (also called the inverse of the discrepancy) of the classical spherical cap $L_2$ discrepancy on the $d$-dimensional sphere $\mathbb{S}^d$. For every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, this bound implies that a single point suffices in all sufficiently large dimensions, which shows a ``blessing of dimensionality'' for the associated numerical integration problem. We then introduce a one-parameter family of distance reproducing kernels for the Sobolev space $H^{(d+1)/2}(\mathbb{S}^d)$. For the balanced kernel $K(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y})=1-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\|\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{y}\|$, a lower bound together with a random-point upper bound shows that the normalized information-complexity is $\Theta_\varepsilon(d)$ for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$. Thus its dependence on $d$ is determined up to constants depending only on $\varepsilon$. Finally, we study the one-sided spherical cap discrepancy obtained by restricting the height parameter to $[0,1]$. We derive its kernel and Stolarsky's invariance principle explicitly. A sharp mean-distance inequality, attained by regular simplices, determines its normalized information-complexity exactly in all sufficiently large dimensions and proves strong polynomial tractability with optimal $\varepsilon$-exponent two.
item.dc:creator: Johann S. Brauchart, Josef Dick, Friedrich Pillichshammer

item.title: Non-Archimedean balanced metrics and their application to totally degenerate abelian varieties
item.description: arXiv:2606.15758v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a polarized complex manifold with discrete automorphism group, it is known that if the first Chern class admits a cscK metric, then the balanced metrics, which are characterized in terms of the algebro-geometric notion of Chow stability, approximate this cscK metric. In this paper, we study a non-Archimedean analogue of this phenomenon. In particular, we prove that such an analogue holds for polarized totally degenerate abelian varieties. As an application, we also show that, for a totally degenerating family of polarized abelian varieties, the validity of this non-Archimedean analogue yields a uniform estimate for the Calabi--Yau metrics on fibers sufficiently close to the degenerate fiber.
item.dc:creator: Keita Goto

item.title: Random Cayley sum hypergraphs and $k$-fold sumsets
item.description: arXiv:2610.08629v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We denote by $f_k(\Gamma)$ the largest integer with the property that every subset of a finite abelian group $\Gamma$ of size at least $|\Gamma| - f_k(\Gamma)$ is a $k$-fold sumset. Extending a recent result of Alon and Pham, we prove that $$ f_k(\Gamma) \leq \widetilde{O} \left(n^{(2k-1)/(4k-3)}\right) $$ holds for all finite abelian groups $\Gamma$ and integers $k \geq 2$, where $n = |\Gamma|$. Additionally, we also show that the lower bound $f_k(\Gamma) \geq \widetilde{\Omega} \left(n^{1/k}\right)$ holds if $\Gamma$ has no nontrivial element of order dividing $k$. Our upper bound improves a previous result of Balogh, Liu, and Sharifzadeh, and recovers the bound of Alon and Pham in the case $k = 2$. The proof relies on a new upper bound for the independence number of random Cayley sum hypergraphs, which may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Jihyo Chae, Hyunwoo Lee

item.title: $2$-Large Sets and Nil-Bohr Recurrence: A Disproof of the $2$-Large Is Large Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.16605v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A set $S$ of positive integers is $r$-large if every $r$-coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ contains arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions with common difference in $S$. We prove that every $2$-large set is a set of nil-Bohr recurrence, i.e., it meets every nil-Bohr neighborhood of $0$. This proves a conjecture of the first author and gives a sharp answer to a question of Host, Kra, and Maass. Furthermore, we show that a piecewise syndetic set is $2$-large if and only if it is nil-Bohr recurrent. From this, we show that a small modification of a set constructed by the first author is $2$-large but not $3$-large, thereby disproving the $2$-large is large conjecture of Brown, Graham, and Landman. We also deduce that the family of $2$-large sets is not partition regular, thereby answering another question of Brown, Graham, and Landman. We also show that, for every fixed nil-Bohr neighborhood $B$ of $0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, restricting the common difference to $B$ increases the extremal number for $k$-term arithmetic progressions by at most a factor of $1+\varepsilon$, provided $k$ is sufficiently large.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Alweiss, Sohail Farhangi

item.title: Relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel of a reductive group over a global field
item.description: arXiv:2611.04773v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe an algorithm and a computer program computing the relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel $Sha^S(K,G)$ of a reductive group $G$ over a global field $K$ with respect to a finite set $S$ of places of $K$ containing no archimedean places. We assume that we know the algebraic fundamental group $\Lambda=\pi_1^{alg}(G)$ together with the action on it of the Galois group $\Theta=Gal(L/K)$, where $L/K$ is a finite Galois extension with no real places such that $Gal(K^s/L)$ acts trivially on $\Lambda$. We also assume that we know the decomposition subgroups $\Theta_v\subseteq \Theta$ for all places $v$ in $S$, and all non-cyclic decomposition subgroups $\Theta_v$ for $v$ outside $S$. Under certain conditions, we compute the set $Sha^S(K,G)$ also when $S$ contains archimedean places.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Borovoi

item.title: PCF All The Way Down
item.description: arXiv:2611.06106v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that a finite surjective post-critically finite self-map of a variety in characteristic zero remains post-critically finite on every preperiodic integral effective divisor after passing to its periodic image with its return map. Iterating this result proves PCF all the way down. A detailed report on AI usage is contained in the manuscript.
item.dc:creator: Taylor Dupuy, Alon Levy, Thomas Tucker, Zhuoran Wang
